Writ petition has been filed under Article 226 of the Con
 of India praying for the issuance of Writ of Mandamus to forbearin
 respondent 2 and 3, its officials, servants, agents or anybody und
 from inteferring with the running of the Petitoners Bunk Shop at N
 Sathiya Dev Avenue, near Open Park, Opposite to Cee Bros, chennai-
 wherein selling Tea, Coffee, Snacks, food and other items, till th
 of Appeal Committee Under Section 20 of the ''Street Vendors (Prot
 of Livelihood Regulation) Act, 2014''.
 For Petitioner : Mr.L.Chandrakumar

For Respondents : Mr.R.Vijayakumar for R1 & R3
 Mr.Raja Srinivas for R2
 Order
[Order of the Court was made by M.SATHYANARAYANAN, J.]

The petitioner, on an earlier occasion, filed W.P.No.14282 of 2020, against the very same official respondents, praying for Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to call for the records relating to the proceedings of the 3rd respondent dated 23.09.2020 and quash the same and consequently forbear http://www.judis.nic.in the respondents 2 and 3, from interfering with the running of the petitioner's bunk shop at No.174,
Sathiya Dev Avenue, near Open Part, opposite to Cee Bros, Chennai 600 028, wherein he is selling tea, coffee, snacks, food and other items.

The Writ Petition was taken up for final disposal on 09.10.2020 and having noted that the provisions of Sub-Section 3 of Section 18 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulations of Street Vending) Act, 2014, have not been adhered to, this Court has directed the Zonal Officer, Zone-13, Adyar, Chennai 600 020, to desist action for a period of thirty days from 25.09.2020 and thereafter, proceed strictly in accordance with law and the Writ Petition came to be disposed of accordingly.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulations of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Now the writ petitioner came forward to file this present Writ Petition to forbear the respondents from any way interfere with the running of the petitioner's bunk shop till the formation of Appeal Committee under Section 20 of the said Act.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that a batch of writ petition has been filed before this Court in W.P.No.32329 of 2020 batch etc., challenging the declaration of non vending zone in Egmore http://www.judis.nic.in area, especially Pantheon Road and Monteith Road and as such, the petitioner may be given a suitable alternative accommodation in the place of choice of the Corporation of Chennai and prays for appropriate orders.

3. Per contra, learned standing counsel appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 would submit that the petitioner has also been vacated from the Bunk Shop in question and admittedly, he is an encroacher and as a matter of right, he cannot seek for alternative accommodation and when the Writ Petition in W.P.No.32329 of 2020 batch etc., decides in favour of the petitioners therein, the petitioner may work out his remedy in accordance with law and prays for dismissal of this Writ Petition with exemplary costs, as it is an abuse of process of Court.

sentences.text: 4. This Court has carefully considered the rival submissions and also perused the materials placed before it.

5. The encroachers nowadays started thinking that it is their fundamental right to encroach upon public lands and put up unauthorised http://www.judis.nic.in constructions and in the case on hand, the only justification is that their livelihood is affected.

This Court can also take judicial notice of the fact that for protection of lawful tenants, there are no laws available except procedural law in the form of Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of CPC and for protecting the encroachers, very many laws are available in the form of Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905 and other allied enactments and thus, the encroachers are getting emboldened.

It is also to be noted at this juncture that the concerned authorities including the Corporation of Chennai, most of the times turn a blind eye,
when the encroachments is being caused and they will be constrained to initiate appropriate action only when some orders are passed in the Writ Petition, despite the fact that they are clothed with all powers to prevent and remove encroachments, but rarely they exercise their statutory functions and developed an habit of abdicating their powers and responsibilities.
6. Now coming to the case on hand, admittedly, the petitioner is an encroacher upon footpath,
which is meant for public and put up bunk shop and also selling food articles
and in the considered opinion of this Court, it http://www.judis.nic.in may be not in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The only point urged by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner is that in the light of declaration of non-vending zone in Egmore area, W.P.No.32329 of 2020 has been filed and the same is pending and till the disposal of the same, by taking into consideration the plight of the petitioner, suitable accommodation may be provided to him.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the said plea made by the petitioner deserves out right rejection.
Being an encroacher, he cannot claim right to pray for alternative accommodation and thereby affecting the public interest and therefore, this Court finds no merit in this Writ Petition.
7. The Writ Petition stands dismissed accordingly.
No costs.
Consequently connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
